args.question: I have to pick one of these moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. Which one actually gives me the best result at the end of the game? I don't really know how to think this many moves ahead.

parts.content:
The best move is **b7**.

Why: it flips the whole 7th row toward **h7**, and more importantly it gives Black the best control of the lower-left corner area. Even though **b7** is normally a scary “next-to-corner” square, here it works because the endgame tactics favor Black after it.

A quick way to think here: don’t ask “what flips most now?”—ask “after my move, can White take a corner or force me into bad corner-adjacent moves?” For this position, **b7** comes out best.

args.question: White just took the a8 corner. Now I can play g2, b6, a7, or c8. Which is best so I don't hand over another corner?

parts.content:
Play **c8**.

It’s the best endgame result here, and it avoids immediately giving White another easy corner. The main danger squares are around the open corners **a1** and **h1**; **g2** is especially close to **h1**, while **c8** is a safer edge move that keeps Black’s position strongest.

args.question: I'm down 22 to 36 now with only 6 empty squares left. My choices are g2, b6, or a7. Is there any way this turns around, and which move should I make?

parts.content:
Play **a7**.

It likely doesn’t fully turn the game around with best play, but **a7 gives Black the best final result**. It looks odd because it’s next to **a8**, but White already owns that corner, so you’re not giving away a new one. **g2** is dangerous because it can help White access the **h1** corner later.

args.question: Only 4 squares left now: a1, h1, g2, a3. My choices are a1, g2, or a3. a1 is a corner - should I take it, or is there a better play here?

parts.content:
Take **a3**, not the corner.

Even though **a1** is a corner, here the move order matters: **a3** gives Black the best finish and avoids letting White control the last few empties more profitably. With only **a1, h1, g2, a3** left, the “automatic corner” instinct can lose value—**a3** is the best endgame play.
